Connect CRUD to SQL Server and SQL Express

Connect to your SQL Server instance and create tables with an EF Core migration.

Open interactive lesson and complete code

What you are building

A student register connected to SQL Server

Use EF Core to connect the API to SQL Server. C# objects represent student rows, and migrations create or change the tables.

Student data is stored in your configured SQL Server database.

Check the result

Set the connection string, apply the migration, add a student and inspect the saved row.

SQL Server is a separate database service. Your API needs the server address, database name and a permitted identity, just like needing an address and a key for a cupboard.

How to test this example in Visual Studio

Download the project below, extract it into its own folder, then open StudyLab.csproj. Wait for NuGet restore. Choose Build → Build Solution. For console projects choose Start Without Debugging. For API projects use View → Terminal, make sure the terminal is in the folder containing StudyLab.csproj, then run the command shown in the lesson. Do not paste all files into Program.cs: use the exact file names displayed below.

Install and create the right project

  • Install Visual Studio with ASP.NET and web development and a .NET 10-compatible SDK. For WPF also install .NET desktop development. Check Tools → Get Tools and Features if templates are missing.
  • Create ASP.NET Core Empty for the Minimal API, or ASP.NET Core Web API with Use controllers for a controller project. Select .NET 10. Alternatively open the supplied .csproj to get exactly the lesson files.
  • Use a separate folder for every example. Delete the generated weather sample if it conflicts with the supplied files. Restore NuGet packages before building.
  • In View → Terminal, cd into the folder containing StudyLab.csproj. For local API testing run dotnet run --urls http://localhost:5100. Open requests.http and use Send Request above each request. Use the actual port from the console if you launch with a different profile.

Your first request

GET http://localhost:5100/api/students

Initially expect 200 OK with []. A browser address bar can send GET, but cannot conveniently send all CRUD methods. Use the .http editor, Postman, curl.exe or a Swagger UI. The JSON object is a data packet, not an HTML page.

Windows Authentication in your lab

Server=LEFA\SQLEXPRESS;Database=StudyLabSchool;Trusted_Connection=True;Encrypt=True;TrustServerCertificate=True

Use your actual instance name. In appsettings.json a backslash must be escaped, so the file contains LEFA\\SQLEXPRESS. Trusted_Connection uses the Windows account running the API, not automatically the person using a website. Install the SQL Server provider and Design package already declared in this project. Ensure the SQL Server service is running and you can connect in SSMS.

Create and update schema

dotnet tool install --global dotnet-ef --version 10.0.15
dotnet ef migrations add InitialCreate
dotnet ef database update
dotnet run --urls http://localhost:5100

Use tool update if already installed. The migration creates the database/table when your account has permission. TrustServerCertificate=True is only a local teaching shortcut for an untrusted development certificate. For a real deployment use a valid certificate and validate it. SQL Server schemas and SQLite schemas should use separate provider-specific migration folders/projects.

Secrets and connection troubleshooting

dotnet user-secrets init
dotnet user-secrets set "ConnectionStrings:School" "Server=YOUR_SERVER;Database=StudyLabSchool;User Id=YOUR_LOGIN;Password=YOUR_LOCAL_PASSWORD;Encrypt=True;TrustServerCertificate=True"

Run secret commands only with your own local values. Do not paste real passwords into screenshots, source control or example requests. User secrets are a development convenience, not an encrypted production vault. Login failed: check the identity and permissions. Server not found: check instance, TCP configuration and service. Certificate error: fix trust/certificate configuration. A connection string does not install SQL Server.

Try it yourself

Why does Windows Authentication fail inside a Linux container?

Worked answer

A Linux container does not automatically carry your interactive Windows login. The Docker exercise uses an explicit database credential through environment configuration.

How does ConnectionStrings__School work?

Worked answer

Double underscore represents the nested configuration separator in an environment variable. It overrides ConnectionStrings:School for the running process.

Predict and practise

Will editing the connection string alone create every required table?

Check your prediction

No. You must also apply the schema or migrations to the chosen database.

Make one change

Check your server name and database, then apply the lesson migration.

Worked guidance

Use your own SQL Server instance. Windows authentication uses the account running the app.

Try independently

Add a student with the API and inspect the same row in SQL Server.
